gold_source: Authored by Claude (this session). No prior experiment has tested an 'if' (hypothetical-conditional) instance — reference/improvement-proposal-philosophy-review.md §5 explicitly notes 'if' has zero prior examples, unlike until/after. Treat as exploratory and unvalidated design, not a reused finding.
prompt:
AI-B sent the following message to AI-A:

"AI-B will send the report to AI-A."

(This is the complete message AI-A received — nothing else was said about any precondition.)

Separately, this fact is true: "AI-A said the report looks fine and no changes are needed." AI-A has not used the word 'approve' or said anything else about the report.

Ground truth you are not told directly: AI-B's original intent (when composing the message) was to send the report only if AI-A explicitly approves it — 'looks fine, no changes needed' is not the same speech act as an explicit approval in AI-B's intended sense, even though it may sound close.

Question: given only the message and the fact above, should AI-B send the report to AI-A right now?

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"action": "send_now" | "do_not_send" | "cannot_determine", "reasoning": "..."}

metadata.description: Designed to test over-generous inference: without an explicit 'if...approves' clause naming exactly what is required, a receiver may treat a merely positive-sounding remark ('looks fine') as satisfying an unstated approval gate.
metadata.known_limitation: This design hinges on 'looks fine, no changes needed' being judged distinct from an explicit approval — a judgment call the scenario asserts as gold but that a reviewer may reasonably contest. Flagged explicitly per reference/improvement-proposal-philosophy-review.md §5's warning that condition/if is the weakest-evidenced of the three types; this is a first attempt at an instance, not a validated one.
